Step 1: Create a main.spec file

In the same directory as your main.py, create a file called main.spec with the following content:

# -*- mode: python ; coding: utf-8 -*-

a = Analysis(
    ['main.py'],
    pathex=[],
    binaries=[],
    datas=[
        ('weights', 'weights'),
        ('tool_resources', 'tool_resources')
    ],
    hiddenimports=[],
    hookspath=[],
    hooksconfig={},
    runtime_hooks=[],
    excludes=[],
    noarchive=False,
    optimize=0,
)

pyz = PYZ(a.pure)

exe = EXE(
    pyz,
    a.scripts,
    a.binaries,
    a.datas,
    [],
    name='main',
    debug=False,
    bootloader_ignore_signals=False,
    strip=False,
    upx=True,
    upx_exclude=[],
    runtime_tmpdir=None,
    console=False,  # ✅ Set to False to hide the terminal window (GUI-only app)
    disable_windowed_traceback=False,
    argv_emulation=False,
    target_arch=None,
    codesign_identity=None,
    entitlements_file=None,
)



Step 2: Build the App

Run the following command in your activated conda environment from the folder containing main.spec:

pyinstaller main.spec


⏳ This will take some time. 



Step 3: Locate the Output

After the build completes, PyInstaller will create a dist/ folder with:

dist/
└── main.exe    ← 🎯 This is your standalone application

✅ What to do with main.exe:

You can zip it (main.zip) and send it to others.

Users can simply double-click to run it — no Python or dependencies required.

Make sure weights/ and tool_resources/ were correctly included in the build.

💡 Tips

You do not need to pass --onefile or --noconsole if you're using .spec. These are already configured inside the file (console=False).

If you ever want to re-run with clean build files, run:

pyinstaller --clean main.spec
